title: TMS Citizenship Essay Contest Details
source_title: IT'S FALL Y'ALL! | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
TMS 

CITIZENSHIP 

ESSAY 

CONTEST TMS CITIZENSHIP ESSAY CONTEST

TMS Citizenship Essay ContestDue October 30, 2026Theme: “If we stop remembering”What could be lost if we stop listening to, sharing, and remembering the stories of our veterans.DIRECTIONS/ FORMAT = You may write an essay, a letter, a poem, a song (any form of writing) based on the theme. Your writing sample should be typed and printed out.YOU CAN NOT JUST SHARE IT WITH A TEACHER. It needs to be printed and turned in to the TMS Office or to Mr. Brinck in room 302. All entries will be mailed to local VFW halls for our veterans to read.Winning entries will be held back and read at the THS Veterans Day breakfast on Wednesday, November 11 at 8am.Prizes -- There will be one winner for each grade level. $50.00 will be placed into their “Travel Account”.The top winner(s) will also have their name(s) placed on a plaque that will hang in the TMS lobby. 1 or possibly 2 winnersRULES: Writing samples are judged on the following: 1- Must be typed & (size 14 font, 1.5 spacing, and “Times New Roman” font). 2- Stick to the topic or theme of the essay.  3- You must print off and turn in a paper copy. You can’t share it on Google Docs. 4- Age appropriate writing. . . IT MUST BE YOUR WORK NOT SOMEONE ELSE!5- Original work . . . please don’t just copy and paste a poem or quote without explaining      the significance to you personally. 5- Correct English and grammar usage(word usage, sentence structure, punctuation, spelling, clarity, flow, etc.)Helpful Hints/Suggestions 1- Make several revisions before you turn in your final copy. 2- Ask someone to read it and offer suggestions to improve it.3- Don’t wait until the last minute. Write a version and wait a day before rewriting/revising. 4- Take pride in your work. Make sure it is your best effort!!Any questions or concerns please contact Mr. Brinck email - brinckj@talawanda.org

summary: TMS is hosting a **Citizenship Essay Contest** with the theme **"If we stop remembering"** about what could be lost if we stop sharing veterans' stories. Students may submit essays, letters, poems, or songs in **size 14 Times New Roman font, 1.5 spacing**, printed and turned in to the TMS Office or Mr. Brinck (room 302) by **October 30, 2026**. Winners receive **$50 in their travel account** and top entries will be read at the **THS Veterans Day breakfast on November 11 at 8am**. All entries will be mailed to local VFW halls for veterans to read. Contact: brinckj@talawanda.org

title: TMS Pie and Butter Braid Fundraiser Sale
source_title: IT'S FALL Y'ALL! | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
TMS 

PTG 

PIE 

& 

BUTTER 

BRAID 

SALE! TMS PTG PIE & BUTTER BRAID SALE!

To Support Class Sponsored Field Trips (Glen Helen & Washington, D.C.)OCTOBER 15th - NOVEMBER 2ndPie Pick up date -- November 18th in TMS Cafe starting @ 2:30pm.Parents & Students,Each year TMS PTG offers two fundraisers. A pie sale in the fall and a cookie dough sale in early spring. The fundraisers are set up so that students have the opportunity to earn money to help pay the cost of class trips offered in the 6th and 8th grade. Every student is welcome to participate and your decision to participate is strictly voluntary. Every student that chooses to participate in a sale will have an account created where their profit will be kept until needed to help pay for a class trip. The pie sale in the fall and the cookie dough sale in the early spring are only meant to help families earn money to help lower the cost of class trips each grade has organized here at TMS. All money raised is held in the student’s account and may be used for any school sponsored trip in 6th or 8th grade. The trips for each grade are as follows:7th Grade = Glen Helen Experience8th Grade = Washington, D.C.Pie Sale = 50% profit & Butter Braids = $6 profit for each one you sell. Your profit total will be deposited into your TMS PTG account. That money may be used to pay for any school sponsored “class trip”. Please read the PTG Fundraising Policy (on the back) for more information.SALE INSTRUCTIONS. . . .STUDENT’S NAME + GRADE on the order sheet(s) - written neatly!Collect all money at the time of sale. Will not process order w/o payment.If it's easier you can keep cash and just submit one check.All checks -- payable to TMS PTG. Place the order sheet(s) and money in an envelope or zip-lock bag. Turn in to the main office or Mr. Brinck in room 302.Note: This fundraiser is voluntary. You are not required to participate. Any questions or concerns about this sale or fundraising in general should be directed to John Brinck. Email = brinckj@talawanda.org Cell  513-477-9503.Pie Facts:All pies cost $18.00 except Pecan $22.00.You will earn 50% profit for all pie sales.All pies are delivered fresh (not frozen). They have a shelf life of 4 to 6 days.7 - 8 days if kept refrigerated.They can be frozen safely for 2 to 3 months.You can reheat the fruit and pecan pies - DON’T REHEAT THE CREAM PIES.Only fresh fruit is used in pies - NO canned fruit.Butter Braid Facts:All Braids (and rolls) cost $18.00.You will earn $6.00 for each butter braid sold. If TMS sells 300+ braids the profit will increase depending on the number sold.All butter braids are delivered frozen, and will last up to 4 months.THERE IS AN ONLINE STORE OPTION FOR BRAIDS.You will have to register yourself to use the online storeThere is a QR Code you can scan to register onlineMore flavors are offered through the online storeTMS PTG FUNDRAISING POLICYSchool fundraisers are designed to assist students wanting to travel on class trips. If a student chooses to not travel (by choice not illness or injury), all money raised is forfeited to the general scholarship fund. There is also a cap to how much profit a student is allowed to earn. The profit stops at $75.00 past the cost of the Washington, D.C. trip. The extra money will be donated to the general scholarship fund. For example: A student earns $700 and the trip costs $600 -- you keep $75 (spending money) and TMS PTG will keep $25. This rarely happens, but we can’t allow students to potentially keep hundreds of dollars in profit.

SEE 

PEACHTREE 

FOR 

ORDER 

FORMS 

AND 

FLYERS! SEE PEACHTREE FOR ORDER FORMS AND FLYERS!

title: Understanding the Green Slip System
source_title: IT'S FALL Y'ALL! | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
WHAT 

IS 

A 

GREEN 

SLIP? WHAT IS A GREEN SLIP?

What is a Green slip?If a student misses a due date for an assignment, they will receive a Green slip. The student's name will be added to a school wide list recording the work that was marked late and the office will call home. The work should be completed and turned in ASAP. Extra help is offered afterschool on Tuesdays and Thursdays until 3:30. If the work is not turned in by the help session, students should stay after. If students did not turn the missing work in after attending the help session, their grade turns to a zero and the work will no longer be accepted.

summary: A **Green Slip** is issued when a student misses an assignment due date. The student's name is added to a school-wide list and the office calls home. Students should complete the work ASAP and can attend **extra help sessions on Tuesdays and Thursdays until 3:30 PM**. If missing work is not turned in after attending a help session, the grade becomes a zero and the work is no longer accepted.

Health Education Curriculum Update - SB 288-Erin's LawThe Ohio Department of Education and Workforce (DEW), formally called the Ohio Department of Education, has shared with public schools across the state Senate Bill 288. This legislation requires that health education curricula be updated to include (K-12/developmentally appropriate) prevention education information in the areas of sexual abuse and sexual violence for students in public schools.As promised, the district is providing an opportunity for families to review the curriculum, and parents may opt their students out of the lessons if they choose.  For more information from the Ohio Department of Education- Click HERE. Instruction occurs annually. This year the district will conduct these updates with students October 12-26, 2026.K-3 Curriculum- Click HERE4-6 Curriculum- Click HERE7-8 Curriculum- TMSSocial Inclusion: Click HEREDating Violence: Click HERESuicide Prevention: Click HERE9-12 Curriculum - THS will share their videos in three successive weeks. Social Inclusion: Click HEREDating Violence / Healthy Relationships: Click HERESuicide Prevention: Click HEREContact your student's building and school counselor with any questions.

summary: The district is implementing **Senate Bill 288 (Erin's Law)** requirements for updated health education curricula covering sexual abuse and violence prevention (K-12). **Instruction occurs October 12-26, 2026**. Families can review grade-level curriculum materials online and opt students out if desired. Topics include social inclusion, dating violence/healthy relationships, and suicide prevention. Contact your student's school counselor with questions.

source_title: September is Here! | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
CLUB 

INFORMATION! CLUB INFORMATION!

ENGINEERING 

AND 

CODING 

CLUB ENGINEERING AND CODING CLUB

After school Engineering and Coding Club starts in September. This is a dynamic and engaging environment where students in 6-8th grade can explore the world of engineering and coding. Our club is designed for students who are interested in technology, problem-solving, and innovation. Two Miami University based clubs will be directing our engineering and coding activities this year. Kode2Learn is a student organization that organizes and runs events for kids in the Oxford area that promote teamwork and problem solving through the use of computer programming. SWE (Society of Women Engineers) organization's goal is to encourage our middle school students to consider engineering or computing as a career and provide activities related to engineering/coding.Engineering/Coding Club times - Schedule(After school until 3:30 p.m.)Engineering Focus: SWENext - Thursdays Sept. 17, 24, Oct. 1, 8, 15Coding/Programming Focus: Kode2Learn - Wednesdays Oct. 21, 28, Nov. 4, 11, 18See Mrs. Ruppert for club permission slips (Room 406).

Permission slips available from Mrs. Ruppert in Room 406.

blocks.content:
LITTLE 

AGGIES! LITTLE AGGIES!

Little Aggies is kicking off for the year! Students interested in agriculture, FFA, leadership, and getting more involved are invited to join us for our first meeting.Wednesday, September 162:15–3:15 PMRoom 301Come see what Little Aggies is all about. All interested students in grades 6-8 are welcome!
